book.echoesofantiquity.lore_book.landing: I did not come here to build.$(br)I came to find out who did.$(br2)$(o)Most of these pages are still blank. The ground gives them up slowly.$()
category.echoesofantiquity.manual.desc: What I have managed to rebuild, and how.
category.echoesofantiquity.architects.de: They measured everything. That is how I know they were afraid.
category.echoesofantiquity.fallen_humans: The ones who went through, and did not come back the same.
category.echoesofantiquity.failed_clones: Someone tried to save people. This is what was saved.
entry.echoesofantiquity.foundations.1: Every ruin I open has the same sherd pressed into its lowest course.$(br2)Not decoration. A $(l)signature$().
entry.echoesofantiquity.foundations.2: Eleven now, across four sites, hundreds of blocks apart.$(br2)Identical. Not similar — identical. They had a standard, and they held to it.
entry.echoesofantiquity.foundations.3: $(o)Later note.$() I was wrong.$(br2)It is a $(l)datum mark$(). Every one sits at the same level, whatever the terrain above.$(br2)They were agreeing on where the world began.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_measure.1: Their tools are all one kind of tool. Tape, level, plumb.$(br2)Nothing for hunting. Nothing for war.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_measure.2: $(o)Later note.$() The gravity anchors bother me.$(br2)You do not build a machine to hold falling stone unless something above is coming down.$(br2)Not builders' tools. $(l)Evacuation$() tools.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_crossing.1: The strongholds all point the same way. Down, and then through.$(br2)They built the frames. They never finished them.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_crossing.2: $(o)Later note.$() The metal is the proof.$(br2)End Steel cannot be worked here. So someone crossed, worked, and $(l)sent it back$().$(br2)The door swung both ways once.
entry.echoesofantiquity.what_came_back.1: Every piece of armour I recover assumes the same thing: $(l)there will be no ground$().$(br2)Straps for falling. Boots that make no sound, because something out there listens.
entry.echoesofantiquity.what_came_back.2: $(o)Later note.$() I made the goggles and looked one in the face.$(br2)It did not attack. It $(l)waited$().$(br2)I have written $(o)stranded$() eleven times in these pages. I am striking it out.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_archive.1: The fragments hum. Hold one long enough and it settles into the rhythm of your own pulse.$(br2)These were not mined. They were $(l)taken$().
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_archive.2: $(o)Later note.$() Ten will wake a waystone, and a woken stone pulls you back from dying.$(br2)Ten. That is not a fuel cost. That is an $(l)exchange rate$().
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_copies.1: The Architects could not evacuate everyone.$(br2)So they did the other thing. They kept what they could of people, and meant to put them back.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_copies.2: $(o)Later note.$() They keep the trade. They keep the craft. They have lost the $(l)hands$().$(br2)A descendant forgets slowly, and unevenly. This is not forgetting.
entry.echoesofantiquity.end_steel.1: Iron will not hold an End charge alone. Bind it to a popped chorus fruit and a pearl and it takes.$(br2)Everything here is built on it.
entry.echoesofantiquity.waypoints.1: The anchor is the destination. Build it once, somewhere you will want to return to.$(br2)The pearl is the journey, and it is spent.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_sieve.1: Their spoil heaps are still full — the leavings of every dig they ever made.$(br2)Nobody ever went back through them. I intend to.

entry.echoesofantiquity.sifting.sand.int: Their dunes were spoil, not desert.$(br2)Everything they dug out, they dumped here.
entry.echoesofantiquity.sifting.gravel.i: Coarser leavings, closer to the shafts.$(br2)Whatever they were mining for, this is what they threw away.
entry.echoesofantiquity.sifting.red_sand: Stained through. I have not worked out by what.$(br2)It gives up different things.
entry.echoesofantiquity.sifting.common.d: Odds of turning up at least once per sift.
entry.echoesofantiquity.sifting.rare.des: Weeks of sifting for one of these.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_sieve.2: It runs on soul fragments. I have stopped asking why.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_sieve.3: Three heaps are worth the work:$(br2)$(l:manual/sifting_sand)Sand$()$(br)$(l:manual/sifting_gravel)Gravel$()$(br)$(l:manual/sifting_red_sand)Red Sand$()
